texts: good. the dated copular clause reifies the new-moon state with the moon as the thing it holds of, carries day 33 and Year 1 on that state, and keeps the flat past form beside it, so both "was the moon new?" and "when was it new?" resolve.

good. the tide's arrival parses as a past event with the tide as the thing that came, and it carries the same day 33 / Year 1 terms as the first sentence, so the two are tied together by date without any ordering being invented.

mixed: the filling itself is right (the spring tide as the doer, the pools as what was filled, past tense), but the plural inside the proper name is lost — "the Salt-bloom Tide-pools" is recorded as ONE thing of kind tide-pool, so nothing says there are several pools and nothing later can point at one of them ("the second pool from the north"). If the individual pools need to be referenceable, introduce them as a set once here: "The spring tide filled the Salt-bloom Tide-pools, a group of five tide-pools."

good. the blooming is a past event located in the tide-pools, and "the tide-pools" is correctly resolved back to the pools named in the previous sentence; "Salt-bloom" is kept as a bare name with no kind atom, which is faithful — the sentence never says what kind of thing salt-bloom is.
good. the overflow is a past event of those same pools, with sundown recorded as its time and no date silently carried over from the earlier dated sentences.
